main_text.p: quuntur,natus;quem nostram scisse linguam non est dubium,ac eam magni fecisse: quippe quâ in tam nobile De natura opus toties inserere voluerit. Ea tamen verba tempo-rum injuriâ adhuc magis depravata apud eum leguntur,nemine de ea lingua ab mille annis curante.Ita lib.18.cap.18.aratra rotulis instructa Gallicum inventum Pflugrat recte nominavit: ubi tamen codices Plumma-rat,alii Planarat habent: quidam in planetas, ut se prorsus ineptos ostenderent, muta-runt. Apud eundem lib.3. cap.16.Bodinetum Padum Gallica lingua à Liguribus dictum ait, quod significet sundo carentem: & Bo-dincomagum oppidum eodem tractatu esse: Helvetiorum lingua vocat Bodenmangel. Padum item à picea arbore, quam Galli ita vocent,nominatum,(quod & M.Porcius Ca-to testatur.)Psch vult dicere, quod adhuc manet in nostra lingua.Ita apud Suetonium in Galba, præpinguis Gallicè Galb intelligi-tur,sed vitulus potiùs.Nam ita præpinguem ac obesum hominem per jocum vitulum vo-camus. Et Beco rostrum apud eundem in Vi-tellio adhuc habent Belgæ nostra ætate in sua lingua:& Helvetii verbum inde Becken, vel Bicken/ id est, rostro ferire. Multa his si-milia enumerat D.Ægidius Tschudus, V.C. apud Helvetios,in libro de Rhætiæ antiqui-tate

page.notes: Transcription uses the printed forms. Several words are in black letter or in a different type within the roman text and are marked with <bl> where clearly Germanic (Bodenmangel, Becken, Bicken, Pflugrat, Planarat, Galb, Beco, Psch). Words such as "Psch" and "Pflugrat" in the first lines are italic or black-letter in the scan; the exact type cannot be confirmed at this resolution, so the spellings "Psch" and "Pflugrat" are copied as seen and may contain an error. The word "Bicken" after "vel" is read as printed; the first letter may be a B or a G. The word "Ea" at the start of the second line is read as printed. The final line ends with "tate" on its own, a catchword-like continuation set to the right; it is treated as the last line of text. Long s is written as plain s throughout. Printed p "scisse" and "si-milia" retain the printed hyphen-less line breaks.
